title: Why More Than 700 Hanok Houses Stand in Downtown Jeonju
mediaSource: Jeonju Hanok Village urban hanok 735 houses history preservation

scenes.title: More than 700 traditional houses sit inside a modern city
scenes.narration: In central Jeonju, more than 700 hanok houses form a dense landscape of traditional tiled roofs.

scenes.title: This is not simply a neighborhood frozen from the Joseon era
scenes.narration: The modern hanok district began taking shape in the early 1900s as Korean-style homes clustered here during a period of rapid urban change.

scenes.title: The city began protecting the area in 1977
scenes.narration: Jeonju designated parts of Gyo-dong and Pungnam-dong as a hanok preservation district and later controlled building height and streetscape.

scenes.title: Officially, 735 buildings are hanok
scenes.narration: Jeonju's current statistics list 947 buildings in the village, including 735 traditional hanok structures.

scenes.title: Traditional culture extends far beyond the architecture
scenes.narration: Historic sites, food, paper, clothing, music, and other local traditions are concentrated in the same neighborhood.

scenes.title: A traditional view shaped by modern urban history
scenes.narration: Jeonju Hanok Village is not just a collection of old houses but a living district shaped by a century of urban change and preservation.
